home.heroCaptionTitle: A steady start. A stronger next step.
home.heroCaptionSubtitle: Good learning grows one day at a time.
home.introTitle: School should help children feel ready to keep learning.
home.introBody: Shri Gurukul Academy is based in New Lepa, Kasrawad, in Khargone district. The academy lists Classes 1–10. We want students to understand their lessons, feel comfortable asking when something is difficult and develop habits they can rely on. Families are part of that work too; a conversation with the school can help make expectations clear.
home.introPoints:
Classes 1–10
Questions are welcome
Practice and steady effort
School–family partnership
home.introAlt: Illustrative students reading books together in a school library.
home.highlightsTitle: The small things that make a difference
home.highlightsSubtitle: Clear explanations, room for questions and regular practice help children build confidence in what they know.

highlights.title: Understand the lesson
highlights.description: Learning sticks when students can explain an idea in their own words, work through examples and ask for help when they need it.
highlights.alt: Illustrative image of a teacher guiding a lesson

highlights.title: Build a steady routine
highlights.description: Short, regular practice gives students a chance to review what they know and notice what still needs attention.

highlights.title: Learn to work together
highlights.description: Listening, sharing ideas and treating classmates fairly matter in a classroom just as much as getting an answer right.
highlights.alt: Illustrative image of students taking part in a team activity

home.valuesTitle: How we treat one another matters.
home.valuesSubtitle: Respect is shown in the ordinary moments: how we listen, how we try again and how we respond to other people.

values.title: Respect
values.description: Listen without dismissing another person and take care of shared spaces and responsibilities.

values.title: Curiosity
values.description: Ask why, look a little closer and be willing to learn something you did not know yesterday.

values.title: Effort
values.description: Keep practising, be honest about mistakes and take the next step instead of giving up.

values.title: Responsibility
values.description: Come prepared, do your share of the work and treat other people’s time and trust with care.

home.leadersTitle: Learning works best when we work together
home.leadersSubtitle: Two things matter throughout a child’s school years: steady support in the classroom and an open line of communication with home.

leaders.message: We want children to know more than the right answer. They should have a chance to ask how it works, practise a new idea and return to a difficult topic without feeling that a mistake is the end of the lesson.

Parents know their children in ways a classroom cannot. When families and the school share questions early and speak plainly about progress, it is easier to agree on the next useful step for a learner.

about.title: About Shri Gurukul Academy
about.subtitle: A school in New Lepa, Kasrawad, serving families looking for clear information and a steady start to learning.
about.heading: A place to learn, try and grow
about.body: Shri Gurukul Academy is based in New Lepa, Kasrawad, in Khargone district of Madhya Pradesh. The academy lists Classes 1–10. We want children to understand what they learn, develop habits that help them work independently and learn to treat others with respect. A school journey is built over time, with effort from students, guidance from teachers and communication with families.
about.sectionTitle: What we want school to feel like
about.sectionSubtitle: The everyday experience matters: being able to ask a question, practise patiently and know where to turn when something is unclear.
about.commitmentTitle: A school relationship built on conversation.
about.commitmentBody: Choosing a school brings practical questions. We want families to have clear, current information and a straightforward way to speak with the school team when something needs explaining.

academics.title: Academics
academics.subtitle: A steady learning journey, from the first foundations to the greater demands of Classes 9 and 10.
academics.calendarDescription: Check the calendar for dates the school has confirmed. For subject lists, books, assessment plans and session-specific guidance, speak with the school office.
academics.levelsSubtitle: The needs of a child in the early classes are different from those of a student preparing for secondary examinations. These stage descriptions are a guide; the school can confirm the current syllabus and subject details.
academics.learningTitle: Good study habits are learned, too.
academics.learningSubtitle: Understanding improves when children have time to practise, useful feedback and a routine they can keep up.
academics.heading: Help knowledge take root.
academics.body: The academy lists Classes 1–10. Across these years, students move from building core reading, writing and numeracy skills to working with more complex subjects and preparing for examinations. The syllabus, subjects, medium of instruction, book list and assessment schedule for the current session should be confirmed with the school.
academics.imageAlt: Illustrative image of students reading together; use an approved academy photograph for the final site.

levels.title: Primary years
levels.description: Reading, writing and numeracy form the base for later learning. Children also practise listening, expressing themselves, following instructions and building a routine for schoolwork.

levels.title: Middle years
levels.description: Subjects become more detailed and students are asked to connect ideas, explain their reasoning, organise their work and take more responsibility for revision.

levels.title: Secondary years
levels.description: Students need a clear understanding of each subject, regular revision and a realistic plan for assessments. Families should follow the school’s published timetable and guidance for the current session.

sections.title: Understand before moving on
sections.description: A student who can explain an idea in their own words has a stronger starting point for the next lesson. Questions and worked examples help make that understanding visible.

sections.title: Practice that builds confidence
sections.description: Short, regular revision is often easier to sustain than last-minute cramming. When a topic remains difficult, the next step is to ask for help and practise it again.

sections.title: Keep families in the loop
sections.description: Parents can speak with the school about progress, study expectations and ways to support a sensible routine at home.

vision.title: Vision, Mission & Values
vision.subtitle: The principles we want students to see in the way people learn and work together.
vision.valuesSectionSubtitle: Values mean most when they show up in everyday choices, not only on a page.
vision.heading: Knowledge matters. So does character.
vision.body: We want school to help students build a sound understanding of their subjects and learn how to use that knowledge thoughtfully. Curiosity, honesty, persistence and respect should be visible in the way we ask questions, approach mistakes and treat other people.

sections.title: Our vision
sections.description: To be a school where children build sound knowledge, ask thoughtful questions and grow into respectful, responsible members of their community.

sections.title: Our mission
sections.description: To support daily learning through clear teaching, regular practice, honest feedback and a working partnership between school and family.

sections.title: Honesty
sections.description: Be truthful about the work you have done, own mistakes and earn trust through your choices.

sections.title: Respect
sections.description: Listen, disagree without putting others down and treat classmates and adults with consideration.

sections.title: Persistence
sections.description: When something is difficult, try another approach, ask for help and give yourself a chance to improve.

sections.title: Curiosity and care
sections.description: Ask questions, stay open to new ideas and notice how your actions affect the people around you.
